chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Not every misled person can be reproved.

key_terms.مَفْتُونٍ: misled person / one bewitched by error

ai.seo_question: Why are some misled people not reproved?
ai.summary: In this saying from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between those who err due to ignorance and those whose hearts are sealed against guidance, implying that reproach (*mu'atabah*) is contingent upon the capacity for acceptance. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *ta'wil* (interpretation of context), where the utility of correction depends on the individual's spiritual receptivity rather than the mere existence of error. It serves as a practical guide for leaders and scholars in tailoring their admonition to the specific state of the recipient.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 15. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Every mischief monger cannot even be reproved. [1]
